# INTRODUCTION 

This document is the User Guide for Product Usage API within the framework of the GSMA Open Gateway initiative, enabling automated usage exchange and settlement between Operators and Channel Partners.

This API is inspired by TMF635 Product Usage API v5.0 for Open Gateway context.

The GSMA Open Gateway initiative defines standardized Service APIs and Service Management APIs, complemented by a common set of Operate APIs that provide cross- cutting commercial and operational capabilities. These Operate APIs define homogeneous integration mechanisms between Operators and Channel Partners to ensure interoperability across networks and markets.

By defining clear and consistent API requirements, this document supports alignment with industry best practices and facilitates communication among stakeholders in the Open Gateway ecosystem. This version focuses on the Usage Consumption Reporting function within the Operate API suite, while future versions may include other Channel Partner integration capabilities such as service assurance, monitoring, and settlement automation.

## OVERVIEW OF GSMA OPEN GATEWAY AND CHANNEL PARTNER MODEL

Open Gateway is a GSMA-led initiative in the telecommunications sector that turns communication networks into platforms by exposing telco capabilities through industry- standard APIs on a global scale under the CAMARA open-source project. CAMARA is hosted by the Linux Foundation and provides the technical framework for these standardized APIs.

Channel Partners are key go-to-market players for Operators that want to sell APIs to many Developers who do not want to integrate individually with each Operator. By aggregating multiple Operators’ APIs into a single Operator-agnostic interface, Channel Partners can offer these capabilities to a wide community of application Developers.

### Channel Partner model overview

Open Gateway Channel Partner model is composed of different players:

- End Users are both subscribers to Operators and users of the application published by the Developers.
- Developers (Application Owner Organization) build and own the applications that consume APIs from the Operators to provide End Users with enhanced features or enable new use cases.
- Channel Partners aggregate Operators' CAMARA standardised APIs to build Open Services and implement Operator end-point routing based on final user identification on the networks.
- Operators expose telco capabilities through CAMARA standardised APIs and could partner with Channel Partners to enable the Services that they offer to Developers.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

An illustrative scenario can involve a game publisher using a cloud provider that acts as a Channel Partner and leverages Open Gateway products such as QoD to enhance mobile gaming experiences. The ability of Operators and Channel Partners to form agreements directly affects which subscribers can access those enhanced services.

Two gamers using the same game but different mobile Operators are mapped to different Operator–Channel Partner relationships, as shown in the relational diagram.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

Example Interaction between players on the model

### Operate APIs

As indicated, the Channel Partner indirect model enables a single channel for tenant applications to gain access to capabilities from multiple Operators, without the need for the customer to set up a contractual relationship with each of them. It is clear the need to provide certain additional functionalities from the Operators to the Channel Partner to enable the commercial model.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

Therefore, in addition to the CAMARA APIs, the Operate APIs are proposed for offering programmable access to Operation, Administration and Management (OAM) capabilities to facilitate the integration of the Open Gateway NaaS Platform with Channel Partner. These APIs provide all the transversal/non-service specific functionalities that are required to make a commercial product out of the Service APIs and Service Management APIs, making them operable and monetizable. Examples of functions provided by the Operate APIs include ordering, usage consumption reporting, monitoring, trouble ticketing, accounting, billing, payment, etc., but also API discovery, user registration and consent management, etc.

**Scope**

This specification focuses on the Usage Consumption Reporting function within the Operate API suite. Its purpose is to define the requirements and aggregated file structure for exchanging ProductUsage data between Operators and Channel Partners. This capability enables automation of the usage collection, reporting, and settlement process, which is essential for monetizing Open Gateway APIs in both the Wholesale Reseller and Marketplace Aggregator models. Operators record each invocation of CAMARA APIs and transform those invocations into ProductUsage records, following the TM Forum Open API and SID information models. These ProductUsage records are then aggregated and shared in bulk with Channel Partners via the Usage Operate API.

**Commercial Models Supported**

| Model | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Wholesale Reseller | The Channel Partner manages the service,defines its own end-user products and pricing,and receives usage data from the Operator forsettlement. |
| Marketplace Aggregator | The Operator defines the product and pricing; theChannel Partner resells it and requires usagedata that already includes rated information forend-user billing. |

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

In both models, the basis of exchange is a structured set of ProductUsage records containing sufficient attributes to enable pricing, billing, and reconciliation. These records are equivalent to CDRs (Call Detail Records) or EDRs (Event Detail Records). The difference lies in whether pricing details are included (Marketplace) or applied later (Wholesale), i.e. rated or non-rated.

**Key Differentiator – What’s New for Usage**

Compared with other Operate APIs such as Ordering, the Product Usage Operate API introduces several specific capabilities.

- A standardized ProductUsage data model aligned with TMF635 v5.0 Product Usage API.
- An embedded ExportJob mechanism for asynchronous bulk data transfer, aligned with TMF635 evolution.
- Defined file and metadata structures using ZIP, JSON and signatures for auditability and interoperability.
- Support for mutual TLS to ensure trusted exchange between parties.
- Compatibility with both Marketplace and Wholesale commercial models.

These differentiators make the Product Usage Operate API a bridge between the commercial product catalog and operational monetization layer. Once APIs are defined and offered in the Operator’s catalog, the Product Usage Operate API provides the mechanism for exchanging measured usage data that directly relates to those catalog entries and pricing models.

**Catalog Alignment**

The Product Usage Operate API complements the TMF936 Open Gateway Product Catalog API by defining how usage of catalogued CAMARA APIs is measured, recorded, and shared between the Operator and Channel Partner. In other words, while the catalog defines what is being offered (e.g., QoD, SIM Swap, Number Verification) and under what commercial terms, the Product Usage Operate API defines how the consumption of those offers is operationally reported and monetized. The two together — catalog definition and usage reporting — form the foundation for automated settlement and revenue assurance across the Open Gateway ecosystem.

The catalog for Operator-exposed APIs includes:

- A CAMARA standardized API available on the Operator’s exposure platform.
- Defined API scopes (e.g., check-sim-swap, verify-number) and corresponding usage characteristics.
- Supported charging models (one-shot, recurring, usage-based).
- Applicable purposes and constraints (privacy, SLA, or policy).

The Product Usage Operate API extends this catalog context by standardizing the ProductUsage exchange for each CAMARA API and aligning usage characteristics with the corresponding ProductUsageSpecification that can be defined in TMF767 Product Usage Catalog API.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

# SAMPLE USE CASES 

Usage refers to the specific instances of Open Gateway API service consumption by end users or applications. These events capture critical data about how, when and by whom a service was used and the products used in the Operator to authorize that service usage. They are the foundational data that drives billing, revenue sharing, and operational insights. Its meticulous tracking and transparent reporting are vital to the integrity and efficiency of modern telecom ecosystems.

In the context of the GSMA Playbook, the Operate API related to Usage are in the context of exchanging data between the Operator and the Channel Partner but could also be considered in the context of a direct relationship between Operator and Developer.

The exchange of information between an Operator and a Channel Partner can be done in a Wholesale Reseller or a Marketplace Aggregator Model:

| Wholesale Reseller Model | Marketplace Aggregator Model |
| --- | --- |
| Services fully managed by the Channel PartnerChannel Partner enters an agreement withOperators for their servicesChannel Partner manages the end user products,performs pricing and invoices developerOperator provides the underlying service andtracks the usageOperator provides the Channel Partner with theusage to support them in billing processes and forreconciliation.Operator provides the service at a wholesale rateand invoices the Channel PartnerChannel Partner deduct a percentage fee to theamount paid by the Developer and make anaccount deposit to the Operator for the remainingamount | Operators upload their products to the ChannelPartner’s Marketplace and enter an agreementfor their servicesChannel Partners provide a unified interface fordevelopers to ensure a coherent user experienceDevelopers purchase products from theMarketplaceOperator provides the underlying service andtracks the usageThe usage is priced according to the Operator’sproduct definitionOperator provides the Channel Partner with thepriced usage required to support them in theirinvoicing processOperator keeps track of their revenue sharebased on the priced usage and invoices ChannelPartner |

For both models, the basis of the information exchange is sufficient details of the use of the APIs to be able to price the event based on required attributes according to the product definition. The key difference between the two types is that the Marketplace Aggregator Model includes how the Operator charged for the CAMARA API usage events based on the product definition. The requirements in this chapter focus on the requirements on the usage consumption exchange between the Operator and Channel Partner for both models above.

## Product Usage Requirements

Each Open Gateway Service API needs its own definition of Product Usage Specification for Wholesale and for Marketplace Aggregator model to exchange information for the Channel Partner to be able to use the data for developer billing, revenue share, and settlement reconciliation (note this is not the settlement in itself, but the data that underpins such an invoice). The difference in the usage event details provided between the two models is that the pricing section is not mandatory in the Wholesale model (could be included depending on the particular agreement between the Operator and the Channel Partner to contain the wholesale rate) but is required for the Marketplace Aggregator model. In this section we enumerate the minimum list of attributes that shall be exposed to the Channel Partner depending on the type of information to be exchanged. This information is considered as the minimum amount of information that would allow Channel Partners to create bills and expose usage to Developers and enable the reconciliation of service usage between Channel Partners and Operators. The usage exchange is at Product level between Operator and Channel Partner, where the Product Usage is built upon internal Operator’s relevant Service Usage events that are not shared with the Channel Partner. As a general principle, due to privacy reasons, the information to be exposed doesn’t include any final user data that could be considered as personal information (for instance MSISDN).

### Exposed usage information to Channel Partners

**Atomic Product Usage Attributes**

Below is the minimum list of attributes of an atomic Product Usage:

Thedate of the APIinvocation ornotification of theservice is part ofthe characteristicsof the usage. | A completionDateattribute has beenadded for moreprecision on theproductUsage datewhen status isfinal. |

Values of the attributes for a given API and operation are defined in characteristics that relate to the Product Usage Specification relevant to the particular CAMARA API. Some characteristics are common across all APIs and should be included in all Product Usage Specs:

- Correlation ID (x-correlator in CAMARA API header) if provided in the CAMARA API request. x-correlator is conditionally mandatory if the x-correlator is provided it has to be included and mapped with a standardized name for it to facilitate interoperability.
- Purpose - For TMF937 first version, we will omit this and add it as needed in future versions of the API.
- Scope - For TMF937 first version, we will omit this and add it as needed in future versions of the API.

Characteristics inherited from the CAMARA API invocation should retain the naming convention from the CAMARA API to facilitate interoperability and understanding. CAMARA API characteristics that are Personally Identifiable Information (PII) or delivery related are not to be included as characteristics.

### Mechanism for Usage Exchange

There is a need to exchange the Usage data between Operator and Channel Partner in an efficient and timely way considering that it is a large volume of data. It needs to support various use cases such as reporting for an Application Owner, internal analytics for Channel Partner, dashboards, operational support including complaints, etc. The key requirement is to provide a mechanism to exchange a bulk of usage data for settlement reconciliation and billing. In the future, online queries and on-demand reporting may be considered.

**Bulk Transfer**

TMF937 adopts a bulk export approach, modeled on the TM Forum ExportJob pattern and aligned with GSMA BCE (Billing and Charging Evolution) practices. This pattern is especially important in high-volume scenarios like CAMARA API monetization.

**Frequency of data exchange**

Operators should be able to export usage records on a regular schedule — such as hourly, daily, or weekly — depending on partner needs and system capabilities. This flexibility allows the model to support both near-real-time usage and end-of-day settlement workflows. In the first version it is assumed that the schedule is part of the Agreement and is set up by the Operator. In future versions we may also include the possibility to set up on-demand subscriptions by the Channel Partner.

**File Structure and Naming Convention**

The exchanged Product Usage is compressed and include both the Product Usage data, metadata and include security through signatures.

**Metadata**

**File Contents**

Each exported file includes zero or more ProductUsage records. If no usage event exists for a reported time period, a file is produced but it contains 0 ProductUsage indicating an empty file. These records reference a ProductUsageSpecification, defined separately in the catalog via TMF936 (planned in a future version), so partners understand how to interpret the usage event characteristics. Records may optionally include pricing details (usageProductPrice) — required in Marketplace Aggregator models where the Operator handles first level rating.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

**Date and Time Stamps**

To ensure consistency and avoid ambiguity across systems and time zones, all dates and times in filenames and attributes are expressed in ISO 8601 basic format (YYYYMMDDThhmmssZ) using UTC (denoted by Z), except fileDateInterval that contains milliseconds for best accuracy (YYYYMMDDThhmmss.mmmZ). This choice eliminates issues with local time zones, daylight savings, and platform-specific filename restrictions, while providing second-level precision and a globally recognized standard for timestamp representation.

**Mutual TLS (Two-Way SSL) Authentication for Report File Consumption**

The system shall enforce two-way SSL (mutual TLS) authentication for all HTTPS requests made to the /exportJob endpoint. This ensures that both the data server and the consuming Channel Partner authenticate each other before any report files are exchanged and that the Channel Partner only has access to the data pertaining to their agreement with the Operator.

- During onboarding, each Channel Partner must register a public certificate with the Operator.
- When invoking /exportJob, the partner must use the corresponding private key to establish the TLS session.
- The server must validate the presented certificate against the registered public key.
- Requests from unrecognized or invalid certificates must be rejected.
- The validated partner identity must be used as a claim in report generation to guarantee the file is associated only with the authenticated partner.
- All report downloads must be served only over authenticated and encrypted connections.

For transferring sensitive files, HTTPS and SFTP can both be very secure if configured correctly, but for pure system-to-system file exchange SFTP is usually preferable because it is purpose built for file operations and naturally encourages strong key-based authentication and end-to-end encryption. HTTPS can be equally strong cryptographically and is the better choice when you need browser access or integration with existing web/API security (OAuth, mTLS, WAFs, etc.).

For now, only SFTP is considered for TMF937 first version.

Download links should always be short-lived and bound to the authenticated API client who requested them by using JWT time-limited tokens. Additionally, access to the file itself must require prior authentication so that the link cannot be used without verifying the API client identity.

**File Retention and Availability**

In the agreement between the Operator and the Channel Partner, the retention period of the files has to be specified. This retention period relates to the period the files are made available to the Channel Partner and not the retention period of the content based on regulation (this is up to the Operator’s policy and local regulation). This is the basis for how the Operator makes the files available in a sliding window for the Channel Partner to consume the files. The retention period of the files is the same as the retention period of the exportJob. Export history is recommended, so previous exports within the pre-defined

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

retention period can be re-accessed.

**Notifications (can be planned for future version)** Operators should notify partners when usage data is available. Channel Partner can subscribe to ExportJob related events via Hub resource or regularly poll the exportJob resource. The notification should include download instructions or a secure link to the file, along with basic metadata (like date range and batch ID).

**Reconciliation between Operator and Channel Partner** For both Wholesale Reseller and Marketplace Aggregator models, sufficient details need to be provided to be able to reconcile the use of the service reported as Product Usage with the amount owed based on the API Usage and product definition. For Wholesale Reseller agreements the Operator invoices the Channel Partner based on the API Usage for a given period at the agreed wholesale rate. For Aggregated Marketplace agreements, the Channel Partner provides a statement of the calculation of the revenue share that is to be deposited to the Operator.

## Use Cases

All use cases apply on Wholesale Reseller and Aggregated models - to any Channel Partner.

### Creation of Product Usage (Pre-requisite) This use case describes the E2E flow of how usage is created to enable the exposure of the usage data to the Channel Partner. It is in the context of TMF937 a pre-requisite to explain the data creation prior to exchanging the data from Operator to Channel Partner.

- Developer invokes a CAMARA API operation via Channel Partner.
- Channel Partner forwards request to Operator.
- Operator invokes the actual service and receives enriched response.
- Operator forwards the response to the application and sends enriched charging request internally.
- Operator charging guides the API to the appropriate product and applies product rules according to the product catalog definition including the definition of the characteristics of the event based on the associated Product Usage Specification.
- A ProductUsage record is created, including:

    - Party identifiers (Application, Channel Partner)
    - CorrelationID
    - API event characteristics
    - Pricing information (if applicable)

## File Packaging, Naming, and Metadata

Defines the physical structure, naming conventions, and metadata content for the ProductUsage bulk exchange files exchanged through /exportJob.

### File Packaging Structure

### Each export job produces a ZIP archive containing:

| Component | Description |
| --- | --- |
| JSON | Zero or more JSON files with ProductUsagerecords. It is the equivalent of the result of a GET/productUsage using the query string passed inthe exportJob query attribute. |
| metadata | JSON file with metadata describing the batch(see schema below). |

### Zip file with its content :

.zip  ¬¬ \*.json

 ¬¬ \*.metadata

The ZIP file contains JSON file(s) and metadata file. The JWS (JSON Web Signature) signature is embedded as a field in the ExportJob (see example above).

### Exception Cases

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

| Case | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Missing ZIP for expected interval | Indicates a missing file in the chronologicalsequence; requires reconciliation. The rules todefine the intervals and contiguity for eachExportJob are based on an agreement betweenChannel Partner and Operator. It is the Operatorthat puts the values in the POST /exportJob foreach ExportJob, so is responsible if there is amissing file. |
| No ProductUsage records produced | ZIP file still created; metadata reports`"numberOfRecords": 0`. |
| JSON too large | Operator and Channel Partner agree onmaximum JSON size or record count; split intomultiple JSON files (`_00001.json`,`_00002.json`, etc.). |
| ZIP too large | Operators may adjust the time interval orcompression level as a mitigation to avoid toolarge ZIP file. (Future enhancement note inrequirements.) |

### File Naming Convention

The `url` and `signature` attributes must reference files whose names comply with the TMF937 file-naming standard defined for ProductUsage ZIP exports.

For zip, metadata and signature:

```
<Status><ReportType><ServingParty><ServedParty><FileDateInterval>[<_SequenceNumber>].<extension>
```

| Element | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Status | C = Commercial, T = Test |
| ReportType | IN (initial); future types TBD |
| ServingParty | 5-character Operator ID |
| ServedParty | 5-character Channel Partner ID |
| FileDateInterval | UTC start–end timestamps (ISO 8601 withmilliseconds) |
| \_SequenceNumber | Only applicable for JSON files. |

Note: The time period (FileDateInterval) is based on the ExportJob query and is also the attribute used to indicate a missed period. For each time period there should be a ZIP file. So the Channel Partner must be able to check if there are missing file date intervals based on the FileDateInterval attribute of all files. There should be no gaps.

### Alignment with Metadata

The metadata file must reflect and confirm all attributes encoded in the filename and referenced by the ExportJob.

| Alignment Element | Source | Validation Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| servingParty | Metadata JSON | Must match ServingParty infilename |
| servedParty | Metadata JSON | Must match ServedParty infilename |
| fileDateInterval.startDateTime /endDateTime | Metadata JSON | Must match FileDateInterval infilename |
| status | Metadata JSON | Must equal filename Statusprefix |
| reportType | Metadata JSON | Must equal filename ReportType |

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

If mismatch occurs, the ExportJob transitions to `status = Failed`, and an error is reported.

### File content

**Product Usage** In the context of **TMF937**, a **ProductUsage** record represents the structured report of a service that has been delivered, guided to a product and is considered billable. It captures the essential information needed for **monetization, settlement, and reconciliation** between an Operator and a Channel Partner.

Each ProductUsage record is defined by a corresponding **ProductUsageSpecification**, which standardizes **what type of usage occurred** (e.g., API call, session, data query) and its associated **characteristics** (e.g., correlation ID, duration, geo scope). This separation ensures consistent modeling across different offers and CSP implementations.

While **ProductUsage is generally agnostic of pricing logic**, its role **depends on the** **monetization model**:

- In a **marketplace aggregator model**, the operator performs the rating, and the ProductUsage record will **include priced values** (e.g., cost, tier applied, currency) to reflect the final charge to the channel partner or developer.
- In a **wholesale model**, the ProductUsage may be exchanged as a processed **usage** **record** with the relevant characteristics, but with pricing determined by the aggregator.

TMF937 ensures that this usage data can be **exchanged efficiently, transparently, and** **interoperably**, supporting:

- Standardized usage structures across parties
- Optional inclusion of pricing context when required
- Accurate and auditable monetization across B2B2X ecosystems In TMF937, ProductUsage is not created or modified by the API — it is _exported_. The Operator’s systems remain the system of record; TMF937 defines only the **format and** **delivery mechanism** for exchanging usage data with Channel Partners. This model enables CSPs to scale participation in Open Gateway by aligning **technical API behavior with** **commercial execution**, and providing the data foundations for **automated rating,** **invoicing, and dispute resolution**.

**TM Forum References:**

- SID ABE: _Product Usage_
- Component : TMFC040 ProductUsage component
- TMF635 v5.0.0 draft — Product Usage Management API (for ProductUsage)
- TMF767 v5.0.0 draft — Product Usage Catalog Management API (for ProductUsageSpecification)
- TMF620 v5.0.0 — Product Catalog Management (for ExportJob)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

**Resource**

The resource that is the basis of the TMF937 API is ProductUsage as defined in TMF635 v5.0.

TMF937 is responsible for exchanging the data between the Operator and the Channel Partner. How the ProductUsage is created and maintained is internal to the Operator and is not applicable for TMF937. What usageProperties that is applicable for a given usage event is determined by the ProductUsageSpecification as part of the ProductOffering.

UsageProductPrice is only required for Marketplace Aggregator model cases where prices are determined by Operator.

| Attribute | Exclusion Rationale |
| --- | --- |
| href | no GET /productUsage operation yet so wouldnot be valued |
| usageType | no requirement |
| usageCharacteristic | replaced by usageProperties for strongly typedcharacteristics |
| relatedParty | no requirement |
| externalIdentifier | no requirement |
| usageSpecification | no need for MVP as the specification ismaterialized in the schema referred viaschemaLocation. May be added in the future ifthere are requirements. |
| serviceUsage | Internal reference to network/service layer usage;not relevant to Channel Partner. |
| usageProductPrice.priceAlterationusageProductPrice.productOfferingPriceusageProductPrice.recurringChargePeriodusageProductPrice.unitOfMeasureusageProductPrice.priceTypeusageProductPrice.name | Simplified out of MVP; price per record capturedin UsageProductPrice if applicable. No need foradditional information. |
| usageProductPrice.price.percentageusageProductPrice.price.taxIncludedAmountusageProductPrice.price.taxRate | Not relevant in B2B2X exchange; all pricing duty-free and tax applied at later billing stages. |

Future versions may consider reintroducing some of these attributes as optional, depending on Open Gateway marketplace models.

**Structure and Relationship**

Each `ProductUsage` record references a ProductUsageSpecification that defines the expected characteristics, such as usage type, reporting dimensions, and correlation keys. TMF937 packages multiple ProductUsage records into a bulk exchange file, accompanied by metadata describing the batch context (period, count, and serving/served parties).

```
ProductUsage 1..* ¬ definedBy ¬ ProductUsageSpecification 1ProductUsage 1..1 ¬ exportedThrough ¬ ExportJob 1
```

**Lifecycle and Exchange Status Policy**

This section defines the valid **status values** for ProductUsage and clarifies **which states** **are eligible for exchange** between the Operator (Serving Party) and Channel Partner (Served Party). The intent is to ensure that only finalized and commercially meaningful usage data is shared, while intermediate or error states remain internal to the Operator.

The standard ProductUsage lifecycle is defined in TMF635, including operational and validation states.

The Product Usage that is to be shared between the Operator and the Channel Partner should be as follows:

| Model | Description | Shared Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **MarketplaceAggregator Model** | Operator performs rating before exchange;shared usage includes monetary values. | rated |
| **Wholesale Model** | Operator shares validated, unrated usage;aggregator/partner applies own pricing. | notRated |

Any other status is of internal interest of the Operator and should not be exchanged with the Channel Partner. The following shows all statuses with comments on relevance:

| Status | Meaning | Exchange Visibility | Comments |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| initialized | Usage recordcreated, validationpending | ❌ Internal | Not complete; not shared |
| rejected | Validation failed | ❌ Internal | Excluded from exchange |
| validated | Format andbusiness rulespassed; ready forrating | ❌ Internal | Pre-rating only |

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

| Status | Meaning | Exchange Visibility | Comments |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| corrected | Correction appliedto a previouslyfailed record | ❌ Internal | May later progress to rated/notRated |
| rated | Successfully rated;final price known | ✅ External(Marketplacemodel) | Included in exchange when Operatordetermines price |
| notRated | Validated but notrated; pricedetermined bypartner | ✅ External(Wholesale model) | Included in exchange when pricinghandled externally |
| failed | Rating failed | ❌ Internal | Operator-only |
| superseded | Usage replaced bya newer record | ❌ Internal | Do not exchange obsolete data |

The filtering of eligible ProductUsage records by status is defined in the `ExportJob.query` parameter of the TMF937 `/exportJob` operation. Example: `query: status=``notRated` ,`rated&completionDate.gte=2025-08-`
`10T00:00:00.000Z&completionDate.lt=2025-09-09T59:59:59.999Z`

In TMF937, only those records with `status=rated` or `status=notRated` are included in the exported file.

**Polymorphism**

In the Open Gateway context, the ProductUsage are modelled using strongly-typed schemas, see more details in ProductUsageSpecification chapter.

**ProductUsageSpecification (not part of the OAS)**

**NOTE** For Open Gateway TMF937 MVP, it has been decided

- to not require exposure of ProductUsageSpecification. The productUsage specification is materialized by the strongly-typed schemas of ProductUsage using polymorphism.
- all Operators have to use standard schemas available in [GSMA-Open-Gateway/Operate-](https://github.com/GSMA-Open-Gateway/Operate-API-References) [API-References: Repository to store schemas and information from the TMF Operate](https://github.com/GSMA-Open-Gateway/Operate-API-References) [APIs. To be read in conjunction with TMF Operate APIs ](https://github.com/GSMA-Open-Gateway/Operate-API-References)for Camara API usages. So that it permits all Operators to use exactly same attribute names for the usage characteristics of each Camara API.
- the definitions of these schemas are done under Operate API stream within TM Forum in collaboration with GSMA
- each Operator can decide to extend the standard schemas with additional attributes if needed, but the standard required ones must be included and not modified (same name and same semantics) to ensure interoperability across Operators and Channel Partners.

**Definition**

A **ProductUsageSpecification** defines the reusable structure, semantics, and measurement dimensions of a ProductUsage record. It acts as the **blueprint** for how a specific type of usage event (e.g., API call, session, query) is captured, identified, and interpreted for charging, analytics, and settlement purposes.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

Each ProductUsageSpecification is:

- **Reusable** across multiple ProductOfferings, even when pricing or allowances differ.
- **Independent** of commercial terms (e.g., tiers, bundles, discounts).
- **Stable** across partners and markets, enabling interoperability and catalog modularity.

In TMF937, ProductUsageSpecification defines the **structure of the exchanged usage** **records**, ensuring that both Operator and Channel Partner interpret the usage data consistently. It is not exchanged dynamically via the API but serves as a **reference** **definition** to interpret ProductUsage attributes within each file.

**TMF References**

- **TMF767** – Product Usage Catalog Management API
- **TMF620** – Product Catalog Management API
- **SID ABEs:** Product Usage Specification, Usage Specification Characteristics

**Business Example**

A single `geo.session.v1` ProductUsageSpecification for a Geofencing API can support multiple offerings:

| Offering | Model | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Basic Geofence | Pay-as-you-go | Charged per session/minute |
| Pro Geofence | Tiered bundle | Monthly allowance + overage |
| Enterprise Geofence | SLA bundle | Fixed-price tier with included usage |

All share the same usage specification (structure, attributes, units), but differ in pricing logic defined elsewhere in the catalog.

**Resource (can be planned for future release)**

See TMF767 v5.0.0 — Product Usage Catalog Management API for details on the ProductUsageSpecification resource.

**Excluded attributes from base schema (can be planned for future release)**

| Attribute | Reason |
| --- | --- |
| serviceUsageSpecification | Internal to Operator; not relevant to ChannelPartner. |
| attachment | Not applicable; no external specificationdocuments required in MVP. |
| specCharacteristic | Not applicable for strongly typed |

**Excluded added to base schema (can be planned for future release)**

No need for extension.

**Product Usage Specification Characteristics**

For MVP, TMF937 defines usage specifications for [Number Verification v1 ](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/camaraproject/NumberVerification/r1.3/code/API_definitions/number-verification.yaml)and [SIM Swap v1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/camaraproject/SimSwap/r1.4/code/API_definitions/sim-swap.yaml) (aligned with CAMARA APIs).

No PII or delivery attributes are included as characteristics.

Each row below represents one _API operation_ mapped to the CAMARA API and its invocation, with non-PII and delivery characteristics included. The reference of the standard characterictis chosen in Open Gateway is the GSMA github repository [GSMA-Open-](https://github.com/GSMA-Open-Gateway/Operate-API-References) [Gateway/Operate-API-References: Repository to store schemas and information from the](https://github.com/GSMA-Open-Gateway/Operate-API-References) [TMF Operate APIs. To be read in conjunction with TMF Operate APIs.](https://github.com/GSMA-Open-Gateway/Operate-API-References) Below you find examples for illustration:

| API | ProductUsageSpecification name | Type ofEvent | Characteristics_(CAMARA attributesminus PII/Delivery)_ | DerivedFrom | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **NumberVerification v1** | OpenGatewayNumberVerificationVerifyProductUsage-v1.0.0 | Atomic | serviceInvocationDateTime, x-correlator,httpStatus (not fornow, could be addedlater if required) | POST/verify | Includes xCorrelator;timestamp in ISO8601 UTC |
| **NumberVerification v1** | OpenGatewayNumberVerificationDevicePhoneNumberProductUsage-v1.0.0 | Atomic | serviceInvocationDateTime, x-correlator,httpStatus (not fornow, could be addedlater if required) | GET/device-phone-number | Same pattern; usedfor device identitysharing |
| **SIMSwap v1** | OpenGatewaySIMSwapRetrieveDateProductUsage-v1.0.0 | Atomic | serviceInvocationDateTime, x-correlatormonitoredPeriod (tobe confirmed),httpStatus (not fornow, could be addedlater if required) | POST/retrieve-date | ExcludeslatestSimChange(non-chargeable) |
| **SIMSwap v1** | OpenGatewaySIMSwapCheckProductUsage-v1.0.0 | Atomic | serviceInvocationDateTime, x-correlator,httpStatus,httpStatus (not fornow, could be addedlater if required) | POST/check | Includes xCorrelator;excludes PII, deliveryattributes, maxAgeand swapped (thelast two are non-chargeable) |

NOTE:

- Characteristics derived from API **response payloads** (e.g., swapped, latestSimChange, device, phonenumber, sink) are typically _not chargeable_ or may be perceived as sensitive PII data or delivery attributes. These types of attributes are omitted from the Product Usage Specfication.
- The characteristics included are request-level characteristics that identify the **invocation** (time, correlation, subscription ID, chargeable attributes) and are retained for TMF937 exchange.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

- For Atomic events the HTTP Response (status) may be optionally included as a characteristic where there is a need to be to distinguish and charge for different outcomes. The norm is that all 200 responses are charged, but there might be cases such as where a request is made but the response cannot be given as a device is turned off (422) where the operator may wish to still see this as chargeable.

Usage type is a classification of usage based on the characteristics, used for reporting, invoice grouping and more. Type of Event defines how a usage event is valued. It reflects the physical or logical dimension that the product

**NOTE** uses to quantify consumption. For MVP we cover Atomic APIs but in the future we will cover also subscription and notification based APIs that may have other requirements.

# SUPPORT OF POLYMORPHISM AND EXTENSION PATTERNS

Support of polymorphic collections and types and schema based extension is provided by means of a list of generic meta-attributes that we describe below. Polymorphism in collections occurs when entities inherit from base entities, for instance an OpenGatewayExportJob inheriting properties from the ExportJob entity.

Generic support of polymorphism and pattern extensions is described in the TMF API Guidelines, Part 2 (TMF630).

The @type attribute provides a way to represent the actual class type of an entity. For example, within a list of ExportJob instances some may be instances of OpenGatewayExportJob. The @type gives this information. All resources and sub-resources of this API have a @type attributes that can be provided when this is useful.

The @referredType can be used within reference entities (like for instance a ExportJobRef object) to explicitly denote the actual entity type of the referred class. Notice that in reference entities the @type, when used, denotes the class type of the reference itself, such as OpenGatewayExportJobRef, and not the class type of the referred object. However since reference classes are rarely sub-classed, @type is generally not useful in reference objects.

The @schemaLocation property can be used in resources to allow specifying user-defined properties of an Entity or to specify the expected characteristics of an entity.

The @baseType attribute gives a way to provide explicitly the base of class of a given resource that has been extended.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

# RESOURCE MODEL 

The Product Usage Operate API works in the Product Usage domain of the TM Forum SID, with ProductUsage and ProductUsageSpecification as the core entities and ExportJob as the mechanism to package and deliver usage externally. File-level metadata and signatures complement these to ensure integrity, traceability and secure delivery between Operator and Channel Partner.

At this time there are no business requirements for exposing individual ProductUsage records via this API; the exposure of ProductUsage in an aggregated file is enough for now and permits to be more efficient due to high volume. There are no business requirements for exposing capability to request an exportJob (the POST exportJob operation is expected to be performed by the Operator’s internal system).

| Entity | Role |
| --- | --- |
| ExportJob | Asynchronous task that selects, packages andexposes ProductUsage data as downloadablefiles. |

## ExportJob

### Definition

An ExportJob represents an asynchronous task that generates and packages finalized ProductUsage records for delivery from a Serving Party (Operator) to a Served Party (Channel Partner).

In TMF937, the ProductUsage Export capability builds upon the TMF635 Product Usage Management API v5.0, which now includes the ExportJob resource as a native, embedded capability, allowing creation, monitoring, and event publication to occur under a single API endpoint (/exportJob).

TMF937 adopts this model and specializes it for inter-party exchange, adding file structure, naming, metadata, and security rules specific to Operator–Channel Partner usage export.

Each ExportJob instance executes a single data extraction based on pre-agreed parameters defined in the Agreement mapped into the selection criteria expressed in the query (time window, status).

(can be planned for future version) When processing completes, an ExportJobCreateEvent notifies the partner that data is available for download.

### TM Forum references

| TMF Asset | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| TMF630 REST Guidelines | Defines the common exportJob resource |
| TMF635 Product Usage Management API | Defines the ProductUsage resource exported bythe job and the common ExportJob resource |

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

| TMF Asset | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| TMF767 Product Usage SpecificationManagement API | Defines the ProductUsageSpecification resource |
| SID ABEs: Product Usage, Product UsageSpecification, Usage Export | Semantic alignment. |

### Purpose in TMF937

In TMF937, the ExportJob is the entity allowing delivering a list of finalized ProductUsage across organizational boundaries. It provides asynchronous, secure, and verifiable data exchange, supporting both Marketplace Aggregator and Wholesale models.

TMF937 exposes in a read-only mode pre-configured exportJobs. The creation and update operations of the exportJob resource are not managed via this API.

An ExportJob:

- Selects eligible ProductUsage records (status = rated or notRated).
- Packages them according to agreed parameters (for instance first productUsage creationDate and last creationDate).
- Generates a downloadable ZIP file containing usage data, metadata, and an optional signature.
- Notifies the Channel Partner upon completion.

## Managed Entity and Task Resource Models

### OpenGatewayExportJob resource

The base class for an ExportJob in the GSMA Open Gateway context, which extends the generic ExportJob class.

**Field descriptions**

**OpenGatewayExportJob fields**

| completionDate | A DateTime. Date on which the job was completed. This attributeexists only when status is Succeeded. |
| --- | --- |
| contentType | A String. The format of the export file. In Open Gateway contextit is always application/gzip. ENUMERATED with values:\* application/gzip |
| creationDate | A DateTime. Date on which the job was created. |
| href | A String. Hyperlink reference. |
| id | A String. Unique identifier. |
| path | A String. JSON Pointer relative to the API root node that pointsto the resource acting as the source for streaming content to theexport destination specified by the ExportJob. Set to/productUsage in Open Gateway context for this API.ENUMERATED with values:\* /productUsage |
| query | A String. Used to scope the exported data. Identical to GET filterconstruct using the API node defined by path as base. In OpenGateway context, contains the query parameters used to filterProductUsage records for export, in particular start and endcompletionDate. |
| signature | A String. JWS (JSON Web Signature) signature of the exportedzip file. Used to verify the authenticity and integrity of theexported data. |

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

| status | A String. Status of the export job. In this context can only beSucceeded. There is no requirement to share non SucceededExportJob. ENUMERATED with values:\* Succeeded |
| --- | --- |
| url | A Uri. URL of the file containing exported data. |
| @baseType | A String. When sub-classing, this defines the super-class. |
| @schemaLocation | A String. A URI to a JSON-Schema file that defines additionalattributes and relationships. |
| @type | A String. When sub-classing, this defines the sub-classExtensible name. |

| Attribute | Description | Comment |
| --- | --- | --- |

### Status Lifecycle (ExportJob.status)

status represents the processing status of the export job itself (distinct from ProductUsage.status)

| Status | Description | (can be planned for futureversion) Event Trigger |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Not Started | Job has been created andqueued for processing. | Triggers ExportJobCreateEvent |
| Running | Data selection and packagingongoing. |  |
| Succeeded | Export completed successfully;file ready for download. | TriggersExportJobStateChangeEvent |
| Failed | Processing failed; no validoutput produced. | Optional ExportJobFailureEvent |

# API OPERATIONS 

Remember the following Uniform Contract:

| Operation on Entities | Uniform API Operation | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Query Entities | GET Resource | GET must be used to retrieve arepresentation of a resource. |
| Create Entity | POST Resource | POST must be used to create anew resource |
| Partial Update of an Entity | PATCH Resource | PATCH must be used to partiallyupdate a resource |
| Remove an Entity | DELETE Resource | DELETE must be used toremove a resource |
| Execute an Action on an Entity | POST on TASK Resource | POST must be used to executeTask Resources |
| Other Request Methods | POST on TASK Resource | GET and POST must not beused to tunnel other requestmethods. |

Filtering and attribute selection rules are described in the TMF REST Design Guidelines.

Notifications are also described in a subsequent section.

### Retrieves a exportJob by ID

### GET /exportJob/{id}?fields=…

### Description

This operation retrieves an OpenGatewayExportJob entity. Attribute selection is enabled for all first level attributes. Filtering may be available depending on the compliance level supported by an implementation.
